sections.summary: This summary provides key information about the MeshCompute utility token. It is intended to support the prospective holder in making an informed decision. The summary covers the offeror, the project, the offer to the public, the rights and obligations attached to the token, the underlying technology, the principal risks, and the environmental impact of the consensus mechanism. The full white paper must be read alongside this summary.
sections.risk_warning: The crypto-asset described in this white paper may lose its value in part or in full, may not always be transferable, and may not be liquid. Past performance of the MeshCompute token is not indicative of future performance. The crypto-asset is not covered by an investor compensation scheme or a deposit guarantee scheme. The risk of total loss is real and the holder should not invest amounts that cannot be lost in full.
sections.management_statement: The management body of the offeror declares that this white paper complies with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCAR), that the information presented is fair, clear, and not misleading, and that no information has been omitted that would be material to the assessment of the crypto-asset. The management body assumes responsibility for the content of this white paper.
sections.notification_date: Date of notification to the competent authority: 2 March 2026 (synthetic fixture date for the reviewer demo).
sections.language: This white paper is drawn up in English, a language customary in the sphere of international finance, and a German-language translation is available on the offeror's project portal.
sections.offeror: MeshCompute Labs UG (haftungsbeschränkt) is a fictional synthetic offeror used only for this local fixture. The fixture legal form is an Unternehmergesellschaft (haftungsbeschränkt) organised under the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, with a fictional registered seat and business address at Example Street 22, 10115 Berlin, and a fictional commercial register reference HRB 000000. Its fictional Legal Entity Identifier (LEI), synthetic and not registered, is 9999SYNTHMESHCMP0151. Investors can contact the offeror at the fictional telephone number +49 30 0000 0000 or the fictional e-mail address contact@meshcompute.example and receive an answer within 5 business days.
sections.issuer: The issuer of the MeshCompute token is the same legal entity as the offeror. No separate issuer exists. The offeror holds the relevant rights to issue the token on the underlying protocol and is registered as described above.
sections.trading_platform_operator: Not applicable. The white paper is drawn up by the offeror. The token is not currently admitted to trading on a regulated trading platform operator.
sections.project: The MeshCompute project develops a decentralised marketplace for verifiable off-chain compute, with the purpose of allowing AI inference workloads to be priced and settled against verifiable execution proofs. The persons involved in its implementation are the offeror's founding team of three engineers with prior experience in distributed systems, ZK proof systems, and high-throughput payments infrastructure. Past and future milestones of the project: the test network went live in January 2026, the marketplace opens with the offer, and third-party compute providers join in 2027. The funds collected pay for development and code audits.
sections.offer_or_admission: The offer is addressed to professional and eligible counterparty customers, and to retail customers in selected European Union jurisdictions for which the offeror has completed the passporting notification. The offer is conducted at a fixed subscription price denominated in euro, in two tranches, with a hard cap on the total amount offered. The target market includes developers and operators of compute-intensive AI workloads. The law applicable to the offer is German law, and the competent courts are those of Berlin.
sections.crypto_asset: The MeshCompute token is a crypto-asset within the meaning of Art. 3(1)(5) MiCAR. Its characteristics: the total supply is fixed at one billion units, recorded in the smart contract documentation, and the token may be transferred between addresses on the underlying protocol with no whitelist restriction. The functionality of the token is to settle protocol fees and to grant access rights to verifiable compute scheduling; both functionalities apply from the start of the offer.
sections.rights_and_obligations: The holder has the contractual right to use the token to pay protocol fees on the MeshCompute marketplace. The holder exercises this right by sending tokens to the fee contract, under the procedure and conditions set out in the terms of service. The holder has no right to redemption against the offeror, no claim against the offeror's assets, and no equity-like rights. The obligations of the holder include compliance with applicable transfer restrictions and the offeror's terms of service. The law applicable to the token is German law, and the competent courts are those of Berlin.
sections.technology: The MeshCompute token is issued on the Ethereum mainnet, a public distributed ledger that uses a proof-of-stake consensus mechanism. The smart contract implementation has been audited by two independent code security firms. Custody of user funds is the responsibility of the user; no custody is provided by the offeror. The protocol is open source and the deployed contract address is published on the offeror's portal.
sections.risks: The principal risks include offer-related risks such as the absence of a deep secondary market after the offer closes, market risk on the token price, project risk including failure of the marketplace to attract sufficient supply or demand, technology risk including smart contract failure and protocol-level bugs, regulatory risk including future changes in MiCAR or AML/CFT requirements, and operational risk including infrastructure outages. Each risk is described in detail in the dedicated risk section of this white paper, together with mitigation measures.
sections.environmental_impact: The consensus mechanism of the underlying protocol is proof-of-stake, which consumes substantially less energy than proof-of-work consensus mechanisms. The offeror monitors the energy and climate-related impact metrics for the underlying protocol as published by independent third parties and publishes the annual environmental and climate-related impact data in line with the ESMA regulatory technical standards on sustainability indicators for distributed ledger technology.

sections.summary: This summary provides key information about the EuroStable asset-referenced token (ART). It is intended to support the prospective holder in making an informed decision. The summary covers the issuer and its authorisation, the referenced assets and the mechanism that aligns the value of the reserve with the claim, the rights of holders including the permanent right of redemption at the market value of the referenced assets, the principal risks, the reserve composition and segregation, the technology, and the redemption procedure. The full white paper, including the management body statement, must be read alongside this summary and is the controlling document for the offer.
sections.risk_warning: The crypto-asset described in this white paper may lose its value in part or in full, may not always be transferable, and may not be liquid. Past performance of the EuroStable ART is not indicative of future performance. The crypto-asset is not covered by an investor compensation scheme or a deposit guarantee scheme. The risk of total loss is real and the holder should not invest amounts that cannot be lost in full.

The management body assumes responsibility for the content of this white paper.

sections.issuer: EuroStable AG is a fictional synthetic issuer used only for this local fixture. The legal form used in the fixture is a stock corporation (Aktiengesellschaft) organised under the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, with a fictional registered seat and business address at Example Street 80, 10115 Berlin, and a fictional register reference HRB 000000. No real BaFin authorisation is asserted; the fixture assumes an ART authorisation field remains under lawyer review. The management body consists of three fictional members with combined prior experience in regulated payment services, treasury management, and information security. Its fictional Legal Entity Identifier (LEI), synthetic and not registered, is 9999SYNTHEUROSTB0184.
sections.art: The EuroStable ART is an asset-referenced token within the meaning of Art. 3(1)(6) MiCAR. Its characteristics: each token gives its holder a claim on the issuer and, where the issuer cannot meet its obligations, in respect of the reserve of assets, and it references a basket of EUR-denominated short-dated sovereign debt instruments issued by Member States of the euro area and of cash deposits at credit institutions authorised in the European Union. Issuance and redemption at the market value of the referenced assets keep its value stable. The persons involved in its operationalisation are the issuer, a fictional technology provider and the fictional reserve custodian. The plans for the token set out its past and future milestones: a closed pilot with authorised participants ended in March 2026, public issuance starts after notification, and admission to a second trading platform is planned for 2027.
sections.offer_or_admission: This crypto-asset white paper concerns an offer to the public of the EuroStable ART. The prospective holders targeted by the offer are professional clients, eligible counterparties and retail customers in Germany and Austria. Tokens are issued at the reference value plus a fixed subscription fee. Admission to trading on a crypto-asset trading platform may follow at the discretion of the issuer. The law applicable to the offer is German law, and the competent courts are those of Frankfurt am Main.
sections.rights_and_obligations: The holder of the EuroStable ART has the following rights against the issuer: a permanent right of redemption at all times in accordance with Art. 39 MiCAR, paid in euro at the market value of the referenced assets, a right to file complaints under the procedure described in Section 9 of this white paper, and information rights regarding the composition of the reserve. The obligations of the holder include compliance with applicable transfer restrictions, sanctions screening, and the issuer's terms of service. The redemption right may not be waived by contract and is enforceable in the courts of the Federal Republic of Germany. The claim each token represents references two assets in specified proportions: 70% short-dated EUR-denominated sovereign debt instruments issued by Member States of the euro area and 30% cash deposits at credit institutions authorised in the European Union. The claim is valued at the market value of those referenced assets: the issuer's middle office values its components daily from independent market prices, and a fictional independent valuation agent reviews the valuation each month.
sections.technology: The EuroStable ART is issued, transferred and stored on a permissioned distributed ledger operated by a fictional third party on the issuer's behalf. Its protocol uses a Byzantine fault tolerant consensus mechanism, and validators receive a fixed fee instead of transaction-based incentives. Smart contract modules govern issuance, redemption, and supply control. Two independent code security firms audited the technology in February 2026 and April 2026, and the audit outcome left no critical finding open. Custody of the technical keys rests with a regulated custodian using multi-party computation.
sections.risks: The principal risks attached to the EuroStable ART are grouped by source. Reserve of assets: if the issuer cannot meet its obligations, holders depend on the reserve, whose market value may fall below the aggregate claims of the outstanding tokens. Issuer: the issuer may fail operationally or financially, including in insolvency, and a sanctions designation of a reserve counterparty may freeze part of the reserve. Offer: the secondary market price of the token may diverge from the reference value, and liquidity may be thin during a redemption surge. Token and referenced assets: the value of the referenced sovereign debt may fall, and credit risk arises on each reserve counterparty. Operationalisation: delays in onboarding authorised participants may disrupt issuance and redemption. Technology: smart contract failure, key compromise or validator failure may stop transfers; mitigation measures include independent code audits, multi-party computation for keys and a tested incident response plan. Reserve impairment events trigger the cure procedure described in Section 11. Redemption may be suspended only under the recovery plan or by the competent authority under Art. 46 MiCAR, and never to manage commercial outcomes.
sections.reserve_of_assets: The reserve of assets is composed of short-dated EUR-denominated sovereign debt issued by Member States of the euro area with residual maturity of less than ninety days, and of overnight cash deposits at credit institutions authorised in the European Union. This synthetic draft states that 30% of the amount referenced in euro is held as deposits with credit institutions. The composition of the reserve is fixed within a defined target band and rebalanced on a quarterly cycle. The mechanism aimed at aligning the value of the reserve with the claim of the outstanding tokens is a daily reconciliation, and any shortfall is restored within one business day. The reserve is held by a separate special-purpose vehicle and is segregated from the issuer's own balance sheet by way of a security trust structure. Custody is provided by a fictional Tier-1 European credit institution acting as qualified custodian under a tri-party custody and segregation agreement. The valuation of the reserve is performed daily at fair value by the issuer's middle office and verified weekly by the custodian. The reserve is audited monthly by an independent statutory auditor and reconciled against the outstanding token supply on a continuous basis through automated supply oracles. Any shortfall triggers the cure procedure described in Section 11 and would be routed to lawyer review for any required authority notification.
sections.environmental_impact: The consensus mechanism used by the issuance protocol is a permissioned Byzantine fault tolerant variant that does not rely on proof-of-work and does not consume energy at the level of public proof-of-work chains. The issuer monitors the energy consumption of the validator infrastructure on a continuous basis and publishes annual environmental and climate-related impact data in line with the ESMA regulatory technical standards on sustainability indicators for distributed ledger technology. Validators source electricity from the European mainland grid, with a contracted renewable share that is reported alongside the annual disclosure. The methodology, scope, and limitations of the climate-related disclosures are described in Annex 2.
sections.redemption: The holder may exercise the permanent right of redemption against the issuer at all times. The issuer redeems by paying euro, other than electronic money, equal to the market value of the referenced assets when the request is processed. The procedure requires a KYC-verified redemption request submitted through the issuer's portal. The timeframe for settlement is one business day from receipt of a complete redemption request, with cut-off at 16:00 CET for same-cycle processing. Redemption is settled by EUR bank transfer to the holder's verified bank account. Redemption is not subject to a fee (Art. 39(3) MiCAR). Only the recovery plan under Art. 46 MiCAR may provide for liquidity fees, limits on daily redemptions or a suspension of redemptions, and the competent authority may temporarily suspend redemption under Art. 46(4) MiCAR; any suspension is published on the issuer's portal.

sections.summary: This summary provides key information about the PayEUR e-money token. It is intended to support the prospective holder in making an informed decision. The summary covers the issuer as an authorised electronic money institution, the par-value redemption right of the holder, the principal risks, the safeguarding of funds received against issuance, and the technology underlying the token. The full white paper must be read alongside this summary.
sections.risk_warning: The e-money token described in this white paper may lose its value in part or in full, may not always be transferable, and may not be liquid. The token is not covered by an investor compensation scheme or a deposit guarantee scheme. The risk of loss is real and the holder should not commit funds that cannot be lost in full.

Holders can contact the issuer at the fictional telephone number +49 30 0000 0000 or the fictional e-mail address contact@payeur-emi.example and receive an answer within 5 business days.
sections.emt: The PayEUR is an e-money token within the meaning of Art. 3(1)(7) MiCAR. Its characteristics: it references the euro, each unit is issued at par value against funds received in euro, and it is intended for use as a means of payment, settlement, and treasury management. A fictional technology provider took part in its design and development.
sections.offer_or_admission: The offer is addressed to professional, eligible counterparty, and retail customers in selected European Union jurisdictions for which the issuer has completed the passporting notification. The issuance is conducted at par against funds received in euro plus the applicable transaction fees. The target market includes payment institutions, merchants accepting on-chain settlement, and consumers seeking euro-denominated digital cash.
sections.rights_and_obligations: The holder has the right to redeem the e-money token at par value against the issuer at any time, with no minimum threshold, in accordance with Art. 49(4) MiCAR. The holder has no right to interest or any benefit linked to the duration of holding the token. The obligations of the holder include compliance with applicable transfer restrictions, sanctions screening, and the issuer's terms of service. The redemption right cannot be waived by contract.
sections.technology: The PayEUR is issued on a permissioned distributed ledger using a Byzantine fault tolerant consensus mechanism. Smart contract modules govern issuance, redemption, and freeze functionality. Custody of the underlying technical keys is provided by a qualified custodian under a multi-party computation key management arrangement. The issuance protocol has been audited by two independent code security firms.
sections.risks: The principal risks are those of the issuer, including its insolvency and the failure of the safeguarding credit institution; those of the e-money token, including redemption delays during operational emergencies; and those of the technology, including smart contract failure or key compromise, with mitigation measures such as independent code audits. Each risk is described in detail in the dedicated risk section of this white paper.
sections.environmental_impact: The consensus mechanism is a permissioned Byzantine fault tolerant variant that does not rely on proof-of-work and does not consume energy at the level of public proof-of-work chains. The issuer publishes annual environmental and climate-related impact data in line with the ESMA regulatory technical standards on sustainability indicators for distributed ledger technology. Validators are hosted on European mainland data centres.
sections.safeguarding: Funds received in exchange for issuance of the e-money token are safeguarded in accordance with Art. 7 of Directive 2009/110/EC (EMD2) as referenced by Art. 54 MiCAR. At least 30% of the funds received is always deposited in separate accounts in credit institutions authorised in the European Union, and the remaining funds are invested in secure, low-risk assets denominated in euro. The funds are not commingled with the issuer's own funds and are protected from claims of the issuer's creditors in the event of the issuer's insolvency.
